title: 6R80 Transmission Support Insulator Removal and Refitting
introduction:
The transmission support insulator is the mounting connection shown above the crossmember. During its removal, temporary support takes over while that connection is apart. I think of the job as a careful handover: the transmission must have its support before the insulator leaves, and its mounting bolts must be tightened before the temporary support leaves.

This procedure applies to the 6R80 automatic transmission identified here. The illustrations distinguish the insulator nuts, the fluid-pan support contact and the insulator bolts; keep those locations separate when matching the tightening instructions.

items.name: Match the transmission and engine
items.detail: Use this procedure for the 6R80 automatic transmission identified in this article.

items.name: Prevent an unexpected start
items.detail:
Begin on a hard, level surface with the vehicle safely parked, the parking brake applied and the wheels chocked. Complete remote-start disabling first, if fitted, through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup. If the menu needs ignition ON, keep a valid key inside and the engine OFF: from ignition OFF, release the pedals and press the start button once; if already ON, leave it ON rather than pressing again.

Establish engine-off ignition ON in the same way if it is not already ON, then hold the service brake and select Neutral in the ground-level cabin. With the parking brake and chocks maintaining restraint, release the brake pedal and press the button once to switch ignition OFF. Confirm ignition OFF and remove the key before hands-on service. Keep the parking brake applied throughout the job.

The ignition controls follow the Ford Mustang owner manual; service precautions are in [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189). A remote or accidental engine start during service can cause serious personal injury or death.

items.name: Personal protection
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection during service and protective gloves when handling pointed or sharp-edged components. Failure to use this protection may cause serious personal injury. See [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

items.name: Capacity and marked contact locations
items.detail: Confirm that the hoist can carry the vehicle’s weight, including cargo and modifications. The lifting reference shows the designated points along the body sides behind the front wheels and ahead of the rear wheels. Locate the triangles stamped into the uni-body sheet metal or frame and position the hoist arms at the designated locations. Lifting elsewhere can let the vehicle shift or fall and cause serious personal injury; incorrect hoist-arm positioning can cause unintended movement and serious personal injury or death. Use [Jacking and Lifting - Overview](#/document/G1663631) to identify the contacts.

items.name: Protect nearby underbody parts
items.detail: Position hoist adapters clear of the suspension, exhaust and steering linkage to avoid damage. On a two-column hoist, keep the forks clear of suspension components, mounting brackets and stabilizer mounting brackets, if equipped, and avoid damaging the axle or rear cover.

items.name: Drive-on lift clearance
items.detail: Before driving onto a drive-on lift, check for interference that could damage the underbody.

items.name: Drive-wheel restriction
items.detail: Do not use the engine to power the drive wheels unless all drive wheels are elevated off the ground. Ground contact can cause unintended vehicle movement and serious personal injury or death.

items.name: Jack restrictions
items.detail: The supplied emergency jack is for changing a deflated tire; using it for other lifting can damage the vehicle. Never apply jack pressure to either bumper because the covers will be damaged. If a jack is used during setup, confirm adequate capacity including cargo and modifications, use a hard, level surface and the designated jacking points, set the parking brake and block wheels remaining on the ground. Support the vehicle with floor stands after jacking and never get underneath while it is held only by a jack, which could lower unexpectedly. Failure to secure the vehicle can cause unintended movement and serious personal injury or death. These precautions do not replace the hoist setup required for this repair.

items.name: Secure the supported assembly
items.detail: Secure the transmission to its support fixture with straps and wooden support blocks. An improperly secured heavy assembly can fall from the fixture and cause serious personal injury. Keep the temporary support in place until the insulator bolts have been installed and tightened.

requirements.category: Lowering and returning to the parked state

items.name: Finish the check before lowering
items.detail: After the support insulator is completely refitted, its bolts and nuts tightened in the stated sequence, and the temporary transmission support removed, remove the remaining tools and clear everyone from underneath the vehicle. Keep the parking brake applied while lowering and restore ground-wheel restraints as the tires meet the ground.

items.name: Restore the grounded parked state
items.detail: With the vehicle fully grounded, chocked and the parking brake still applied, restore its parked gear. Enter the ground-level cabin with the valid key, release the pedals and press the button once from known ignition OFF for engine-off ON. Hold the service brake, select Park, then release the brake and press the button once for OFF. Confirm ignition OFF and remove the key before leaving.

edits.why: The equipment table remains the preparation checklist for the temporary transmission support.

edits.text: With the vehicle in NEUTRAL, position it on a hoist at the designated lifting points. Refer to: Jacking and Lifting - Overview (100-02 Jacking and Lifting, Description and Operation).
edits.why: The linked reference identifies the body-side lifting points by their stamped triangles. Those marked contacts establish where the hoist supports the vehicle; the temporary transmission support serves a separate purpose.

edits.text: Remove the transmission support insulator nuts shown beneath the center of the crossmember. During installation, after the insulator bolts are tightened and the temporary transmission support is removed, install these nuts and tighten them to 59 lb.ft (80 Nm).
edits.why: The drawing distinguishes these nuts from the insulator’s mounting bolts. Their tightening operation comes later in the reverse installation sequence.

edits.text: NOTE: Position the jackstand and wooden block so that the support bears on the outer rib of the transmission fluid pan.
edits.why: The support view and its close-up identify the outer rib as the required contact location, rather than an arbitrary point on the pan.

edits.text: Support the transmission with a jackstand and a wooden block at the specified outer-rib contact before removing the insulator bolts. Use the General Equipment: Vehicle/Axle Stands. Use the General Equipment: Wooden Block.
edits.why: This temporarily carries the transmission while its insulator is detached. The wood sits between the stand and the identified pan contact; the support must remain in place through insulator refitting and bolt tightening.

edits.text: Remove the bolts securing the transmission support insulator, then remove the insulator. During installation, refit the insulator and tighten these bolts to 76 lb.ft (103 Nm) while the temporary transmission support remains in place.
edits.why: The mounting view identifies the bolts above the crossmember. Completing their tightening before removing the temporary support restores the mounting connection in the required order.

edits.text: Reverse the removal sequence. Refit the transmission support insulator and install and tighten its bolts to their stated installation torque while the transmission remains supported. Only after those bolts are tightened, remove the temporary jackstand and wooden block. Then install and tighten the insulator nuts to their stated installation torque. Finally, lower the vehicle from the hoist.
edits.why: This completes the support handover in order: the insulator bolts are tightened first, temporary support is removed next, and the nuts are installed and tightened afterward. Do not postpone bolt tightening until after removing the support.
